messages:
Priya Shah: quick sanity check — onboarding an int8 build of redwood-small on A100 across aws/gcp/azure (same sku) and seeing p95 latency delta ~12-18% and throughput drop on GCP at higher concurrencies. anyone else hit weird tail divergence after driver bump?
Miguel Torres: saw something similar last month after we bumped cuda from 11.8->12.1 on one GCP pool. p50 unchanged, tail moves. :thinking_face:
Sam Lee: can you paste the exact kernel/cublas versions and the workload profile? small model, seq len?
Priya Shah: seq=512, batching continuous, warm prefix cache enabled, steady-state traffic. drivers: AWS(A100): nvidia-driver 525.116 + cuda 11.8; GCP(A100): nvidia-driver 535.54 + cuda 12.1; Azure(A100): 525.116 + cuda 11.8.
Jun Park: hmm GCP is the odd duck here. did you check GPU clock governor / power limits? some GCP images toggle boost differently under sustained workloads.
Miguel Torres: also check mig vs non-mig? but you said same sku non-mig. Could be cublas/cuBLASLt kernel fallback in 12.x for int8 paths.
Priya Shah: confirmed non-MIG. attaching small perf dump:
```
# perf summary (steady-state, conc 24)
region aws gcp azure
p50 12.3ms 12.7ms 12.4ms
p95 24.1ms 28.4ms 25.0ms
qps 410 350 400
```
Miguel Torres: that p95 jump + qps drop on GCP suggests microstalling or kernel choice change. run `nvidia-smi topo -m` and `dmesg | tail -n 50` for OOM/therm throttles. also try setting `TF_ENABLE_CUBLASLT=0` for a quick A/B.
Priya Shah: running checks now. infra-bot: allocating debug VMs in us-central1 for a repro.
infra-bot: created instance gcp-debug-197654 for Priya Shah (link: https://internal/instances/gcp-debug-197654).
Sam Lee: if env var flip helps, then it is kernel selection. if not, likely driver / firmware interplay. can you capture `nvprof` or `nsys` short trace? small run for ~30s should show kernel names.
Priya Shah: quick nsys run attached — saw a lot of `cublasLtMatmul` on AWS/Azure but `cublasMatmul` and some `sgemm` fallbacks on GCP. copying snippet:
```
# snippet from nsys
kernel: cublasLtMatmul algo=lt_gemm_batched
kernel: cublasMatmul algo=sgemm_fallback
```
Jun Park: that aligns with cuda 12 changing heuristics. try forcing `CUBLASLT_ALGO` override or downgrade driver on test host. Also check MSI-X interrupt generosity — cloud NIC drivers sometimes starve PCIe interrupts which can exacerbate tail.
Miguel Torres: i recommend two quick experiments:
- run with `TF_ENABLE_CUBLASLT=0` (or model runtime equiv) to force legacy path and compare p95/qps
- boot a GCP custom image with nvidia-driver 525 + cuda 11.8 (match AWS/Azure) and run identical sweep
If both bring parity, it's driver/kernel selection. If neither fixes, we dig deeper on firmware/NUMA.
Priya Shah: ran first test `TF_ENABLE_CUBLASLT=0` -> p95 down to 25.6ms and qps to 390 (much closer). will spin up the matching driver image next. :thumbsup:
performance-bot: automated-scan report: linked perf run 197654 — p95 delta GCP->AWS = +17.9% (seq512, conc24). flagged as "kernel-fallback-suspect".
Sam Lee: OK this is actionable. MIG to create a short playbook:
- temp env var to mitigate
- create ticket for driver/partner engs with nsys traces + nvidia driver versions + sample config
- add regression alert to perf dashboard if p95 gap >10% across same sku/driver tiers
Priya Shah: creating ticket now and sharing traces: https://redwood-internal/perf/197654
Miguel Torres: thanks — ping me on the ticket, i'll help with kernel heuristics and a small repro script to force different cublasLt algorithms.
Priya Shah: cheers everyone. followup after driver test (will post numbers). :eyes:
